goal: A player in the EEA/UK is asked for ad consent before any ad SDK touches their device, can find the policy, consent re-prompt and support contact from a Settings sheet, never sees a fake "TEST AD" panel, and meets a listing on both stores that actually describes the game — while ad pacing stops resetting on every cold start.
non_goals: Building an IAP ladder or any consumable/currency economy. Block Blast's ~$66k lifetime IAP against ~$1M/day ads (evidence brief) says placement tuning beats an SKU ladder at this stage; a single remove-ads SKU is escalated, not planned.

Adding an analytics or crash-reporting SDK. Every new SDK re-opens the Data safety form, the privacy policy vendor list and the consent scope. W7-12 gets its baseline from LevelPlay's own dashboard/impression data instead.
Shipping banner or native ad formats (the SDK exposes LevelPlayBannerAdView / LevelPlayNativeAdView). 'The board is sacred' in PRODUCT.md rules a persistent banner out of the game screen.
Making iOS shippable. W7-17 specifies only the ads/privacy prerequisites; the native board view compile is the iOS workstream's (docs/IOS_BOARD_PLAN.md).
Changing the reward economy (hint / +1 heart continue). Rewarded is the retention-positive format already in use; W7 does not touch its placement.
Server-side anything: no remote config, no cloud save, no backend. Every step here is client + store console only.

steps.title: Consent state module + LevelPlay privacy API wiring (CMP-agnostic half)
steps.what: Add /Users/gentlegen/Desktop/Projects/arrows-game/src/ui/consent.ts exporting a small, UI-free consent state: `type ConsentState = { gdprApplies: boolean; personalisedAds: boolean; ccpaOptOut: boolean; resolved: boolean }`, a `loadConsent()`/`saveConsent()` pair backed by SaveSystem ints (see the migration note in RISK), and `applyConsentToAdSdk(state)` which calls, in this order, `LevelPlayPrivacySettings.setCOPPA(false)`, `LevelPlayPrivacySettings.setCCPA(state.ccpaOptOut)`, and `LevelPlay.setConsent(state.personalisedAds)` — all three exist in node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation/lib/typescript/src/models/LevelPlayPrivacySettings.d.ts and .../src/LevelPlay.d.ts:36 and are today never called anywhere in the repo (grep -rn 'setConsent|GDPR|CCPA|COPPA' src/ returns 0 hits). Then restructure src/ui/ads.tsx:154 `initAds()`: it must take a resolved ConsentState as an argument, call applyConsentToAdSdk BEFORE `LevelPlay.init(request, …)` at src/ui/ads.tsx:174, and return early without initialising at all when GDPR applies and the user refused. App.tsx:35 currently fires `initAds()` unconditionally inside the boot effect — change it to await the consent gate (W7-02) first.
steps.why: Legal exposure, not optimisation. app.json declares com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID and plugins/withLevelPlay.js injects play-services-appset / play-services-ads-identifier / play-services-basement, so the shipped binary reads advertising and app-set identifiers with no lawful basis captured anywhere. Unity's own LevelPlay docs state the privacy APIs should be set before SDK init (6.14.0+) and that consent must be obtained before initialising the ad SDK — https://docs.unity.com/en-us/grow/levelplay/sdk/react/regulation-advanced-settings and https://docs.unity.com/en-us/grow/levelplay/platform/legal-resources/ironsource-gdpr-compliance (read 2026-09-09).
acceptance: With consent refused, `LevelPlay.init` is never called: a release-candidate build with a temporary `console.log` at each privacy call plus `adb logcat` over a full cold start shows the three privacy calls and NO '[ads] LevelPlay init success' line, and no interstitial or rewarded ad is ever shown in that session (the rewarded button reports failure and the lose panel still offers Retry — the existing degrade path at src/ui/ads.tsx:297).
With consent granted, logcat shows setCOPPA → setCCPA → setConsent all emitted BEFORE the '[ads] LevelPlay init success' line, in that order, on the same cold start.
Consent survives a cold start: after granting, force-stop and relaunch; logcat shows the same three calls with the same values and no consent UI.

A unit test in src/ui/__tests__/consent.test.ts asserts loadConsent() returns resolved:false on a virgin int store and returns the saved triple after saveConsent(), using the existing MemoryStore path in src/core/saveSystem.ts.
steps.verification: `npx eas build -p android --profile preview` → install the APK on a physical Android device (NOT the emulator: the perf emulator has no Play Services ad stack) → `adb logcat -c` → cold start → drive one clear and one loss → `adb logcat | grep -E '\[ads\]|\[consent\]'`. This exercises the original failure directly because the failure IS 'the SDK initialises and reads the ad ID without any consent call ever executing' — the log ordering on a real cold start is the only artifact that shows the call order the SDK actually saw. Jest cannot close this: the native module does not exist under ts-jest/node, which is exactly why the bug survived to now.
steps.risk: If the consent gate throws or hangs, ads never initialise and rewarded hints/continues silently stop working. Ship behind an exported `CONSENT_GATE_ENABLED` constant in src/ui/consent.ts, default ON but flippable in one line, and wrap applyConsentToAdSdk in the same try/catch style already used in src/ui/ads.tsx:242 so a privacy-API rejection degrades to 'no ads' rather than a crash. PERSISTED-STATE MIGRATION NOTE: three new int keys — arrows_consent_resolved, arrows_consent_personalised, arrows_consent_ccpa — packed as 0/1 ints, so the INT-ONLY store interface (getInt/setInt/deleteKey in src/core/saveSystem.ts) does NOT need widening. They MUST be appended to the frozen PersistenceKeys array in src/core/saveSystem.ts or they will never hydrate (src/ui/storage.ts hydrates exactly SaveSystem.persistenceKeys via multiGet), and the exact-array assertion at src/ui/__tests__/storage.test.ts:36-46 will fail until updated. Wipe risk: NONE — purely additive, absent keys read as the getInt default (0 = unresolved = show the consent flow), and SaveSystem.resetProgress() must NOT delete them (consent is not progress).

steps.title: Consent UI: integrate a Google-certified CMP (decision escalated in W7-E1)
steps.what: Add the actual consent screen behind the state module from W7-01. Recommended path: add Google's User Messaging Platform via a CMP module, call its gather-consent flow once at boot from App.tsx (after fonts/save hydrate, before initAds), and map its result into ConsentState. LevelPlay 7.7.0+ automatically consumes GDPR consent from Google UMP and registered CMPs supporting Google Additional Consent (https://docs.unity.com/en-us/grow/levelplay/sdk/react/regulation-advanced-settings), and this repo runs unity-levelplay-mediation 9.2.0 / IronSourceSDK 9.4.0.0 (package.json, node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation/unity-levelplay-mediation.podspec) — so the explicit setConsent from W7-01 becomes belt-and-braces rather than the only channel. The consent form must NOT be a full-screen branded takeover of our own design: a CMP form is the CMP's UI. Our only owned surface is the re-prompt entry point in Settings (W7-04).
steps.why: Legal exposure. GDPR/UK-GDPR require consent before an ad SDK reads device identifiers, and Google requires a Google-certified CMP integrated with IAB TCF for serving Google demand to EEA/UK/CH users (https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13554116, https://support.google.com/adsense/answer/13554116). This binds hard the moment W7-13 adds an AdMob adapter; until then GDPR still binds for the ironSource/Unity demand source itself.
acceptance: GATE 0 (do this first, it can kill the whole approach): the chosen CMP module compiles and runs on Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86.3 with newArchEnabled=true (android/gradle.properties) — evidenced by a successful `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:android --variant release` and the app reaching the menu. Its RN 0.86 / new-architecture support is UNVERIFIED as of 2026-09-09 and must be established before any other work in this step.

On a test device forced to EEA geography via the CMP's debug-geography setting, a consent form appears exactly once on first launch, before the menu is interactive, and never again on subsequent cold starts.
Choosing 'reject all' in that form results in the W7-01 refusal path: no init, no ads, gameplay fully playable including Retry after a loss.
Outside EEA/UK (no debug geography), no form appears and ConsentState resolves with gdprApplies:false — the non-EEA player's flow from splash to Play is unchanged in tap count.
steps.verification: Physical Android device, release-variant build, CMP debug geography forced to EEA, `adb logcat -c` then cold start; capture (a) a device screenshot of the consent form, (b) the logcat ordering from W7-01, (c) a second cold start showing no form. Screenshot is required because this is a UI surface and this project has a scar from UI changes verified only by tsc. Forcing debug geography is what makes the EEA branch reachable from a non-EEA test device — without it the branch is untestable and any 'it works' claim is unfounded.
steps.risk: HIGH integration risk: a CMP module is a new native dependency on a project that pins an exact Expo/RN matrix, and one of the two candidate wrappers is a thin community package. Rollback = the CONSENT_GATE_ENABLED constant from W7-01 plus removing the dependency; because /android and /ios are gitignored (.gitignore 'generated native folders'), removal is a package.json + app.json plugin-list revert followed by prebuild, with no hand-edited native files to unwind. If GATE 0 fails, escalate W7-E1 rather than hand-rolling a consent dialog: a self-built dialog is not a Google-certified CMP and does not satisfy the AdMob requirement.

steps.title: Interstitial pacing: persist the counter, add a wall-clock cooldown, a session cap and a new-player grace
steps.what: src/ui/ads.tsx:255 `let finishedGames = 0` is a module-level in-memory counter, so it resets on every cold start; a player who leaves between levels — the session shape PRODUCT.md describes — effectively never sees an interstitial. Replace it with a small policy object in a new src/ui/adPolicy.ts exposing pure, unit-testable functions over an explicit input record `{ finishedGames, lastImpressionEpochSec, impressionsThisSession, totalSolved, nowEpochSec }` returning a boolean, so the decision is testable under the existing node-env ts-jest setup (jest.config.js testMatch is **/__tests__/**/*.test.ts). Wire four rules: (1) the every-N-finished-games counter, now persisted; (2) a wall-clock cooldown since the last impression; (3) a per-session impression cap; (4) a new-player grace keyed off the ALREADY-PERSISTED SaveSystem.totalSolved so no extra key is needed for it. Also fix the ordering bug this exposes: src/ui/ads.tsx:269 returns before checking readiness but src/ui/ads.tsx:274 resets the counter only on the native path, while the fake path at :288 resets unconditionally — after W7-03 removes the fake path from production, make the reset happen exactly once, only when an ad actually displayed.
steps.why: Revenue (the counter reset is lost inventory) AND retention: Li et al. KDD 2021 (14,615 vs 14,687 users) establishes that early-session friction dominates churn for players in their first days, which is what the grace period protects. The specific pacing numbers are NOT specified here — see RISK.
acceptance: Cold-start persistence, the original failure: finish one level, force-stop the app, relaunch, finish a second level — an interstitial is shown at the point the policy says it is due. Evidenced by logcat showing the policy inputs and the LevelPlay display callback across the two processes. Today this sequence shows nothing, ever.

The cooldown holds across a cold start too: immediately after an impression, force-stop, relaunch, and finish enough levels to satisfy the counter — no ad until the wall-clock cooldown has elapsed (verified by two runs, one inside and one outside the window, with the device clock untouched).

Unit tests in src/ui/__tests__/adPolicy.test.ts cover each rule independently plus the boundary at exactly the cooldown value and exactly the grace threshold, using injected `nowEpochSec` (no timer mocking, no Date.now in the pure function).
With W7-03 in place and no ad available, the counter is NOT consumed: two consecutive due-but-unfilled 'Next level' taps followed by a filled one still show exactly one ad.
steps.verification: Physical-device release build, logcat trace of the policy inputs/outputs across a force-stop boundary (`adb shell am force-stop com.danteb.arrows`), plus `npm test` for the pure policy. The device run across a force-stop is what exercises the original failing path — the whole defect is that process death resets the counter, which no unit test on the current in-memory variable can observe.
steps.risk: PERSISTED-STATE MIGRATION NOTE: two new int keys — arrows_ad_games_finished (small int) and arrows_ad_last_impression (epoch SECONDS; ~1.79e9 today, inside int32 until 2038, so the INT-ONLY store needs no widening). Both must be appended to the frozen PersistenceKeys in src/core/saveSystem.ts or they never hydrate (src/ui/storage.ts multiGets exactly that array), and the exact-array assertion at src/ui/__tests__/storage.test.ts:36-46 must be updated in the same commit. Wipe risk: NONE, additive; absent keys read 0, which the policy must treat as 'no impression yet' (not 'impression at epoch 0 → cooldown long expired' — that is the same behaviour here, but state it in a comment so a later signed-diff change does not invert it). SaveSystem.resetProgress() should NOT clear the ad keys — a progress reset must not become a way to farm ad-free play. NUMBERS: the cooldown, session cap and grace threshold are NOT specified in this brief because no measurement exists to derive them — this project has been burned 6+ times by unmeasured targets. Ship them as named constants in src/ui/adPolicy.ts with values set by the owner as an explicit product decision (W7-E5), and tune only after W7-12 provides a baseline. Rollback: the policy module is pure and the call site is one function; reverting to the old behaviour is a one-line change, and the persisted keys can stay (harmless).
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no arrow is animated, nothing leaves the static layer, no Skia node added — the change is entirely in ad scheduling, and the interstitial is a native full-screen surface outside the React tree. PASS. Brand gate: 'no timers' in PRODUCT.md refers to gameplay timers; a wall-clock ad cooldown is invisible to the player and adds no on-screen countdown.

steps.title: Establish an ad baseline from LevelPlay's own data before tuning anything
steps.what: Before changing any pacing value, capture a ≥7-day baseline from the LevelPlay dashboard for the live build: impressions/DAU, ARPDAU, rewarded fill and completion rate, and interstitial show-rate per placement, plus D1/D7 retention if the dashboard exposes it. Where dashboard granularity is insufficient, the SDK already exposes LevelPlayImpressionData (node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation/lib/typescript/src/models/LevelPlayImpressionData.d.ts) — impression-level revenue data available WITHOUT adding an analytics SDK. Record the baseline in a dated docs/ad-baseline-<date>.md the way docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md records perf runs, including the sample size (sessions and days) next to every rate.
steps.why: Every pacing number in W7-11 and every claim about a placement change is otherwise an invented threshold. This project's memory lists unmeasured targets in briefs as a 6×-repeated failure; this step is the measurement that a later tuning brief must cite.
acceptance: The baseline document states, for each metric, the value, the date range, and the number of sessions/users it was computed over — a rate quoted without its denominator does not count.

Interstitial show-rate is reconciled against expectation: (interstitials shown) vs (levels finished × the policy's expected rate). A gap here is the direct measurement of the W7-11 cold-start defect and should shrink after it ships.
No new third-party SDK appears in the dependency dump from W7-06 as a result of this step.
steps.verification: Dashboard exports (CSV) filed with the document, plus — if impression-level data is used — a logcat capture showing the impression callback firing on a device. The reconciliation line is the honesty gate: this project's memory records four separate occasions where a percentile was quoted over an unverified sample count.
steps.risk: The dashboard's own attribution windows can make two metrics disagree; note discrepancies rather than picking the flattering number. No runtime risk if impression data is only logged in __DEV__.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no motion; optional listener registration only. PASS. Brand gates: none.

steps.title: Give the waterfall more than one demand source (revenue; drags compliance behind it)
steps.what: Today 'mediation' has exactly one demand source: the ironSource/Unity SDK itself — node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation ships no third-party adapters and plugins/withLevelPlay.js injects only play-services-appset / ads-identifier / basement, no adapter artifacts. Adding networks is two-sided: (a) LevelPlay dashboard — enable the networks and set floors; (b) binary — add each adapter's Android dependency through a new config plugin alongside plugins/withLevelPlay.js (NOT by editing android/, which is gitignored and regenerated by prebuild), and each adapter's Pod for iOS later. Every adapter added also expands: the privacy-policy vendor list (W7-05), the Data safety mapping (W7-06), and — if AdMob is among them — makes a Google-certified TCF CMP a hard requirement rather than a recommendation (https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13554116).
steps.why: A single-source 'waterfall' has no competition, so eCPM is whatever one network offers. This is the highest-leverage revenue item that does not touch the player experience at all.
acceptance: `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath` on a fresh prebuild lists each intended adapter artifact — proving the config plugin actually injected them, since /android is regenerated and hand edits vanish.

The LevelPlay Test Suite (already reachable via the unwired `launchAdTestSuite()` at src/ui/ads.tsx:230 — wire it to a __DEV__-only affordance) reports every enabled network as integrated on a physical device; screenshot filed.

Post-launch, a ≥7-day window compared against the W7-12 baseline reports eCPM and ARPDAU with the impression count for each period stated next to it. Do not report a lift whose two periods have overlapping ranges or wildly different sample sizes.
The privacy policy vendor list and the Data safety mapping are updated in the SAME release as the adapters, not after.
steps.verification: Gradle dependency report on a clean prebuild + LevelPlay Test Suite screenshot on a device + the dashboard comparison with sample counts. The Test Suite is the network's own integration check, which is why it exercises the thing being changed; a green build only proves the artifacts resolved.
steps.risk: Each adapter is native code with its own privacy behaviour, its own proguard needs (the app.json extraProguardRules block would need extending — it currently keeps com.ironsource.**, com.unity3d.** and the AdMob surface) and its own store-declaration consequences. Adding AdMob without a certified CMP in place first is a compliance regression, so this step MUST NOT ship before W7-02. Rollback: remove the plugin entry from app.json's plugins array, prebuild, rebuild — no hand-edited native state.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no motion. PASS. Brand gates: adapters must not introduce banner or in-board formats — full-screen interstitial and rewarded only, so 'the board is sacred' holds.

steps.title: Play listing screenshots — there are none, and Play requires at least two
steps.what: Capture at least 4 portrait phone screenshots from a release-variant build on a physical device: the menu (wordmark + Play + stats line), a mid-level board on a recognisable silhouette (a Heart or Cat level — the audit lists Heart@162, Cat@168), a dense SuperHard board showing the fit-to-view advantage, and the win panel. Store them under store/screenshots/ with the device and build id in the filename, and add a short capture recipe to RELEASE.md. Do NOT use the PERF_MODE path for this: src/perfMode.ts boots straight into 'game' and disables persistence/ads, so the menu and win panel are unreachable there. The existing adb capture helper in scripts/perf/android/benchmark.mjs:1400-1410 (`adb -s <serial> exec-out screencap -p`) is the mechanism to reuse; drive the game by hand.
steps.why: Play will not publish a listing without ≥2 portrait screenshots and the repo has zero (store/ holds only feature-graphic.png, playstore-icon-512.png and marketing/ brand art). Play policy also expects screenshots to show real gameplay — the marketing/board-*.png renders are generated boards, safe as supporting art but not a substitute.
acceptance: ≥4 PNGs at the device's native portrait resolution, each showing real in-app pixels from a release-variant build (no mockup frames, no composited copy).

At least one shows a dense board where the whole board is visible in one screen — this is the review-evidenced advantage over the incumbent (their reviews complain they cannot see the whole board), so it should be the second screenshot in listing order.
Both themes are represented (Ink Night and Daylight), since the theme toggle is a differentiator and the listing should not imply a single look.
The capture recipe in RELEASE.md names the exact adb command and states that PERF_MODE must be OFF.
steps.verification: The PNG files themselves, plus `adb shell getprop ro.product.model` and the build id recorded in the filenames/README so a third party can tell which build produced them. Screenshots are the deliverable here, so the artifact is the evidence.
steps.risk: Screenshots taken from a debug build can show a dev overlay or the TEST AD panel — capture only after W7-03 has landed, from a release variant.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no code change to motion. PASS. Brand gate: no confetti/glow compositing over the captures; PRODUCT.md's anti-references apply to store art as much as to the app.

steps.title: Two listings, two copy sets — and a title that is not the word 'Arrows'
steps.what: Write store/listing/play.md and store/listing/apple.md (versioned in-repo, so listing changes are reviewable like code). Play indexes the title (30), the short description (80) and the FULL description (4000) for search, so the long description should carry the search-relevant vocabulary naturally. Apple indexes roughly the app name (30) + subtitle (30) + a 100-character keyword field ≈ 160 characters total and does NOT index the description at all — so the Apple copy must front-load in the name/subtitle/keywords what the Play copy can spend paragraphs on. Fix the title: the bare word 'Arrows' competes with every arrow app on both stores; RELEASE.md already anticipates 'Arrows: Ink Night' as the fallback. The three defensible claims from the audit — infinite procedurally generated levels (the incumbent is finite and handcrafted), the whole board always visible, a distinct night/ink identity — are the copy's spine.
steps.why: Discoverability is the cheapest growth lever available to a solo Android-only game, and the two stores' indexing models are different enough that one copy set cannot serve both.
acceptance: Every field is inside its store's character limit, and each file states the limit next to the field with the character count — checked mechanically, e.g. `awk` over the file, not by eye.

The Play title is not the standalone word 'Arrows'; if the app.json `name` field changes, the change is reflected in app.json AND the Play Console listing AND the adaptive-icon label, and a device screenshot shows the launcher label.

No claim in either file contradicts the audit: the copy must NOT say 'find the order' or imply order-dependent puzzle-solving — the audit's 50 random-greedy playthroughs across 10 levels showed every board clears in exactly arrowCount taps with zero dead ends, so PRODUCT.md's 'the puzzle is finding the order' is false as implemented and must not become a store claim.
The age/audience posture in the copy matches W7-07.
steps.verification: Character-count check over the two files, a launcher screenshot if the app name changes, and a line-by-line pass against the audit's factual claims list. The false-claim check matters because a store description asserting a mechanic the build does not have is both a review risk and the source of one-star 'not what it said' reviews.
steps.risk: Changing app.json's `name` changes the launcher label and, if done carelessly, the Play listing identity. It does NOT change the package (com.danteb.arrows) so installs and the LevelPlay app registration are unaffected — state that explicitly in RELEASE.md so nobody re-registers the ad units.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no motion. PASS. Brand gate: copy must read calm/minimal — no 'CRAZY FUN!!' hyper-casual register, which is PRODUCT.md's named anti-reference.

steps.title: Settle icon and screenshot questions with the stores' free A/B surfaces, not taste
steps.what: Use Play Console's store-listing experiments (free, console-side, no code, splits real store traffic and reports install-rate with significance) to test: (a) the current Higgsfield feature-graphic/icon pair versus the script-composed alternative, (b) screenshot order — dense-board-first versus menu-first. Run one variable at a time. Apple's equivalent, Product Page Optimization (up to 3 treatments, free), is available only once an iOS app is live, so it is gated behind the iOS workstream. Record each experiment's hypothesis, dates, traffic and result in docs/listing-experiments.md.
steps.why: The evidence brief's brand/art questions (which icon, which screenshot leads) are taste-based, and the harness rule is to escalate taste rather than guess — except where the store hands you a free, real-traffic A/B that answers it with data.
acceptance: Each experiment record states the hypothesis, the single variable changed, the start/end dates, the installs per arm, and the console's own significance verdict — a winner declared without the console's significance readout does not count.
A losing variant is recorded as a loss and not quietly re-run with a different framing.
No experiment runs concurrently with another listing change (a copy edit mid-experiment invalidates it) — the document records what else shipped in each window.
steps.verification: Console experiment result screenshots filed with the document. Nothing here is verifiable from the repo; the brief says so rather than implying a local check exists.
steps.risk: Play experiments need enough store traffic to reach significance; with low daily visitors an experiment may never conclude. Record 'inconclusive at N installs over D days' as the outcome rather than picking the higher number — this project's memory has a scar for percentiles quoted over unreconciled sample counts.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no code, no motion. PASS. Brand gate: any variant tested must still satisfy PRODUCT.md's anti-references; an experiment is not a licence to test a hyper-casual treatment.

steps.title: iOS ads prerequisites (ATT, SKAdNetwork, and a currently-false privacy manifest) — ship with the iOS workstream
steps.what: Three concrete gaps, all needing config plugins because .gitignore lists /ios and /android under 'generated native folders' — hand edits to ios/ are erased by the next prebuild. (1) ios/Arrows/Info.plist has no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and no SKAdNetworkItems array; both are required for an IronSource-linked build to serve and attribute ads on iOS. (2) ios/Arrows/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy currently declares `NSPrivacyTracking = false` and an EMPTY `NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes` array — untrue for a binary linking IronSourceSDK 9.4.0.0 plus IronSourceAdQualitySDK (both present in ios/Pods/), and Apple validates privacy manifests at submission. (3) The ATT prompt itself needs no new dependency: unity-levelplay-mediation exports ATTrackingManager with getTrackingAuthorizationStatus/requestTrackingAuthorization (node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation/lib/typescript/src/utils/ATTrackingManager.d.ts) — so expo-tracking-transparency is NOT required. Wire the ATT request after the GDPR consent step from W7-02 and before initAds, and only on iOS.
steps.why: Without these the iOS build is rejected or serves unattributed ads at gutted eCPM. It is sequenced last because iOS is not shippable regardless — the native board view has not compiled since the 2026-09-01 exit protocol change (docs/IOS_BOARD_PLAN.md).
acceptance: After `npx expo prebuild --clean -p ios`, the REGENERATED ios/Arrows/Info.plist contains NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and a non-empty SKAdNetworkItems array, and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy declares NSPrivacyTracking true with the collected data types matching the ad SDK — proving the config plugin owns these, not a hand edit that prebuild would erase.
On an iOS device/simulator running the built app, the ATT prompt appears exactly once, AFTER the GDPR step, and the returned status is logged; a denied status still leaves the game fully playable.
The SKAdNetworkItems list matches the ad networks actually enabled in the waterfall (W7-13) — a stale list is an attribution loss, not just cosmetic.
steps.verification: `npx expo prebuild --clean -p ios` followed by `plutil -p ios/Arrows/Info.plist | grep -E 'SKAdNetwork|NSUserTracking'` and `plutil -p ios/Arrows/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, then an on-device/simulator run with a screenshot of the ATT prompt. The prebuild --clean is essential: it is the only check that proves the plugin regenerates the values, which is exactly the failure mode a hand-edited ios/ would hide until the next CI build.
steps.risk: UNVERIFIABLE with today's tooling in one respect: the iOS app cannot be built end-to-end until the native board view compiles (docs/IOS_BOARD_PLAN.md gates A1-A5, ≥20 GB free disk), so the ATT prompt and SKAdNetwork attribution cannot be observed on a real iOS build yet. Closing that needs the iOS workstream plus a Mac with the disk headroom and an Apple developer account. Do not mark this step done on a successful prebuild alone.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: no arrow animated, no static-layer change, no Skia node. PASS. Brand gates: ATT is a system prompt; nothing of ours is drawn.

escalations.question: W7-E1: Which consent management platform do we integrate — Google's UMP through a React Native wrapper, or a different Google-certified CMP with an RN SDK?
escalations.options: (a) Google UMP via react-native-google-mobile-ads (largest community, but a big dependency that also pulls the whole AdMob SDK, and its RN 0.86.3 / new-architecture support is UNVERIFIED as of 2026-09-09); (b) a UMP-only thin wrapper such as react-native-ad-consent or react-native-google-ump (much smaller surface, both also unverified against Expo SDK 57 / newArch, and lower maintenance confidence); (c) a commercial Google-certified CMP with an RN SDK (paid, but support and TCF 2.3 maintenance are someone else's problem); (d) do not serve ads at all in EEA/UK for now — geo-gate the SDK off and keep the rest of the world.
escalations.recommendation: Start with (b) or (a) behind GATE 0 in W7-02 — build it on a branch, run `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:android --variant release`, and let the compile decide before any integration work. LevelPlay 7.7.0+ automatically consumes GDPR consent from Google UMP and registered CMPs, so a UMP-based choice gets the mediation-side plumbing for free; our own setConsent from W7-01 stays as a belt-and-braces channel either way. Option (d) is a legitimate temporary answer if the build gate fails and revenue from EEA is small — it is far better than shipping ads there without consent — but it needs the geo determination to come from the SDK/CMP, not from a locale guess.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It turns on facts I could not verify without building: whether any of these modules compile against Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86.3 with newArchEnabled=true, and on the owner's willingness to pay for a commercial CMP.

escalations.question: W7-E2: Do we get the privacy policy, the Data safety answers and the DSA trader declaration reviewed by someone legally qualified before the next release?
escalations.options: (a) yes, a one-off review of the three artefacts produced by W7-05/W7-06/W7-09; (b) no, publish the engineer-drafted text and accept the risk.
escalations.recommendation: (a), scoped tightly to those three artefacts. These are the only items in W7 whose failure mode is regulatory or listing removal rather than lost revenue, and the review is one-off rather than ongoing. If the answer is (b), at minimum do not let the policy claim anything the binary contradicts — W7-06's artifact-derived mapping is what makes that check possible.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It is a legal-risk-appetite and budget decision about the owner's own trader status and liability, not a technical one.

escalations.question: W7-E3: Do we stay 13+ target audience, or pursue under-13 reach?
escalations.options: (a) 13+ target audience, COPPA flag false, AD_ID retained, current ad stack unchanged; (b) under-13 or mixed audience — requires COPPA true, dropping the AD_ID permission, a families-policy-compliant ad configuration, and likely a different demand mix at much lower eCPM.
escalations.recommendation: (a). RELEASE.md already assumes it, the current SDK stack is built for it, and (b) would invalidate W7-01, W7-05, W7-06 and W7-13 simultaneously. The calm night-time positioning in PRODUCT.md is not a children's-product positioning either.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It is a product-audience decision with a revenue consequence, and it changes which compliance regime the whole workstream targets.

escalations.question: W7-E4: Do we add a single remove-ads IAP, and if so when?
escalations.options: (a) never; (b) after the W7-12 baseline exists and ad ARPDAU is known, so the SKU can be priced against measured lifetime ad value; (c) now, alongside the compliance work.
escalations.recommendation: (b). Block Blast's ~15M DAU at ~$1M/day on ads against ~$66k LIFETIME IAP is strong evidence that placement tuning outranks an SKU ladder at this stage. It also adds real cost here: expo-in-app-purchases/RevenueCat is a new dependency, a new store configuration, a purchase-restore surface in the Settings sheet (W7-04 leaves a slot), and a persisted entitlement in an INT-ONLY store. Not (c) — it would compete for attention with items that can get the listing removed.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It is a monetisation-strategy decision, and its timing depends on a baseline that does not exist yet.

escalations.question: W7-E5: What initial values do the interstitial cooldown, per-session cap and new-player grace take?
escalations.options: Any set of three numbers; e.g. a cooldown in minutes, a cap of N impressions per session, and a grace of the first N levels solved (readable from the already-persisted SaveSystem.totalSolved).
escalations.recommendation: Set them as an explicit, owner-chosen starting policy — recorded as such in src/ui/adPolicy.ts comments — and treat W7-12's baseline plus a post-change comparison as the thing that justifies any later value. I deliberately do NOT propose numbers: no measurement in this repo supports one, and this project's memory records six-plus occasions where an unmeasured threshold in a brief produced an unreachable or nonsensical target. The one directional constraint the evidence does support is that the grace should be generous for brand-new players (Li et al. KDD 2021: too-hard/high-friction early experience carries ~3× the churn hazard of too-easy for players in their first days).
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: There is no live measurement to derive the values from, and the trade-off between revenue and early-session friction is the owner's call.

open_verification_gaps: W7-02's CMP module compatibility with Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86.3 / newArchEnabled=true is UNVERIFIED. My web search returned no compatibility statement for these versions. Closing it requires a branch build: `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:android --variant release`.

No physical Android device has ever been used on this project (all perf numbers are from one API 31 emulator, per project memory). Every ad/consent acceptance criterion in W7-01, W7-02, W7-03 and W7-11 requires a real device with Play Services — the emulator's ad stack is not equivalent, and the perf harness sets animator_duration_scale=0 which is not a normal runtime. UNVERIFIABLE until a device is available.

Whether LevelPlay 9.2 requires the privacy calls strictly before init, or merely recommends it: Unity's docs state 'set the API before initializing' as best practice for 6.14.0+ and require consent before initialising the SDK, but I have not seen a hard error path for the reverse ordering. W7-01 implements the strict ordering regardless; the residual unknown is only whether the looser ordering would also work.

Whether the current live listing already has screenshots and declarations that differ from the repo. I can read the repo (store/ has zero screenshots) but not the Play Console. W7-09 and W7-16 are owner-attested by dated console screenshots and cannot be closed from here.
Whether GitHub Pages is actually serving docs/privacy-policy.html at the URL RELEASE.md predicts. Unverified — W7-05's acceptance closes it with a curl against the live URL.

targetSdkVersion 36 is INFERRED, not proven for the shipped bundle: node_modules/expo-modules-core/android/ExpoModulesCorePlugin.gradle:69 defaults it to 36 and a stale local lint model records 36.0. W7-08 closes it with bundletool against the actual .aab.
The revenue effect of W7-11 and W7-13 cannot be predicted from anything in this repo. Both must be reported as before/after windows with impression counts, never as a projected lift.

iOS end-to-end verification of ATT and SKAdNetwork (W7-17) is blocked on the iOS board-view compile (docs/IOS_BOARD_PLAN.md) and needs a Mac with ≥20 GB free plus an Apple developer account. A successful prebuild is NOT sufficient evidence.
